assessments.statement: controller.compute_budget_saturated: The newly read plan records match the proposal's retain condition: optimization_raw_status is User_Requested_Stop at sampled updates 8, 24 and 28 (F662, F669, F690) with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible at update 8 (F684), and update_wall_s runs 11.5-28.1 s against the 0.01 s control period, with deadline_misses unchanged at 35 in both runs. Selected iteration 0 at sampled updates 0, 16 and 24 (F696, F702, F712) indicates the accepted plan is the feasible-return/seed plan rather than a converged one. These are controller-side plan records, not backend motion, so budget-limited plan selection remains a plausible, not certified, contributor.

assessments.statement: solver.termination_limited: Sampled updates terminate by User_Requested_Stop (F662, F669, F690) or Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded (F667) with optimization_selected_iteration in {0, 68} (F696, F702, F712, F635), all below the configured max_iterations 120 (F525); the weaken condition (Solve_Succeeded reaching convergence) was not observed. Convergence is not the stopping mechanism in the sampled records, so the termination-limitation explanation is retained; the record is a plan value and does not by itself establish physical causality.

assessments.statement: tendon.force_limit_saturation: The newly read applied tensions match the proposal's weaken condition: the maximum sampled channel value is 7.999998299677138 N at update 30 (F699) and 7.999987676698501 N at update 32 (F680), i.e., at or below the 8.0 N per-tendon limit (F346), and both runs record force_bound_violation_n 0.0. Sampled loading approaches but never exceeds the limit, which argues against actuator-limit saturation driving the hold-speed failure; the 27 unqueried updates and the unqueried force_limit_saturated flag leave it only partially tested rather than refuted.

hold.tip_speed_penalty_insufficient: The sampled records show holding_tip_speed_weight 0.05 present in the recipe (F538) but expose no per-term cost contributions, so the sufficiency of the penalty cannot be assessed from the plan records — the proposal's stated unresolved condition. In addition the effective_horizon is truncated to 7, 5, 3 and 1 at updates 28, 30, 32 and 34 (F640, F691, F711, F681), i.e., over the interval overlapping the final holding window, so the holding cost is being applied over a shortened horizon there. This neither confirms nor refutes penalty insufficiency; the hypothesis stays unresolved.

check.authorization: Current frozen diagnosis request; no production change or backend execution.
expected_observations: Sampled updates report optimization_raw_status = User_Requested_Stop with update_wall_s far above the 0.01 s control period.
Sampled updates predominantly report Solve_Succeeded with effective_horizon = 10 inside the control period.
Sampled updates terminate by User_Requested_Stop or Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded with optimization_selected_iteration below max_iterations 120.
Sampled updates report Solve_Succeeded with optimization_selected_iteration reaching convergence.
Sampled actual_tension_n stays at or below the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.
Sampled actual_tension_n reaches or exceeds the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.
Sampled plan records show accepted plans with the raised holding_tip_speed_weight present but expose no per-term cost contributions.
check.proceed_if: The sampled plan records separate the competing explanations directly: optimization_raw_status and optimization_selected_iteration show whether solves end by requested stop (compute budget) rather than convergence, effective_horizon shows whether the terminal/holding horizon is truncated relative to the configured 10, and actual_tension_n shows whether per-channel loading approaches the 8.0 N limit. A late-run pattern of User_Requested_Stop with truncated effective_horizon would retain the compute-budget/solver-termination explanations while leaving the tip-speed-penalty explanation as the residual, whereas a converged full-horizon solve with tensions inside the limit would point to cost design rather than compute budget — a distinction not obtainable from the sampled summary alone.
check.proposal: Do the retained per-update plan records show systematic budget-driven early solver termination and/or a truncated effective_horizon across the run (especially the final holding window), and do per-channel applied tensions stay within the 8.0 N limit — thereby distinguishing a compute-budget/solver-termination limitation from the insufficient hold tip-speed penalty as the explanation for the sampled holding-speed failure?
check.revise_if: Interpret the received result against the declared outcomes.
check.stop_if: Stop after the single plans-view query returns the sampled per-update records or reports the entry unavailable.; Stop when the sampled records establish whether raw solver status and effective_horizon are systematic and whether sampled tensions stay within the 8.0 N limit, or when coverage is reported missing.; Stop within wall_s 180 and one tool call; no numerical check, backend solve, or production change.
weakening_observations: Sampled updates predominantly report Solve_Succeeded with effective_horizon = 10 inside the control period.
Sampled updates report Solve_Succeeded with optimization_selected_iteration reaching convergence.
Sampled actual_tension_n stays at or below the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.

policy.computation: Reported separately; never substitutes for reach or holding acceptance.
policy.objective: Raw scalar objectives under different weights are not ranked.
policy.rule: Joint acceptance first; otherwise componentwise physical comparison.
policy.tradeoff: Any physical improvement accompanied by physical worsening is a trade-off, not overall improvement.

coverage.definition: Both endpoints, timestamps aligned to task sample_period_s; missing samples are unavailable, never a pass.

duration.definition: Final closed interval [task duration - window, task duration].

position.definition: Maximum sampled world tip position error in the final interval.

speed.definition: Maximum sampled world tip translational speed norm in the final interval.
Euclidean norm of tip-site translational Jacobian times recorded backend qvel, reconstructed with sealed robot.xml and qpos; no finite differencing

terminal.definition: Euclidean world tip position error at the final execution sample; sealed evaluate.reach is the outcome authority.

control_period.definition: Simulated control spacing; synchronous wall overruns do not imply skipped applied updates or injected actuator delay.

duration.definition: Simulated task horizon, separate from computation wall time.

timing.interpretation: Applied updates, initialization selections, simulated duration and measured wall time are separate facts.

spendable.reservations: Running/unknown calls are charged at reservation until sealed; included once in ledger usage.

unmet_criterion: Historical joint reach/holding acceptance is false; exact criteria are host-bound.
